title: Suspended or debarred by the City, and on a City contract team afterwards
question: Does any firm on the City's suspension and debarment reports appear on a City contract that began after the City acted?
finding: 33 firms on the City's suspension and debarment reports were tested. 1 firm appears on City contract teams that began after the City acted: Kwan Wo Ironworks Inc.. Kwan Wo Ironworks Inc. is listed as a subcontractor on 4 Public Works contracts that began between 19 December 2024 and 19 February 2026, $3.4 million agreed to it and $452,237 recorded as paid; 4 of the 4 began before 1 March 2026, the end date printed for the debarment. The Controller's reports list a suspension of the firm, its owner and SFR Recovery Inc. "issued and effective on 3/1/2021" (6 reports, June 30, 2021 to December 31, 2023); the reports from June 30, 2024 to December 31, 2025 instead print "Florence Kong, Kin Wo Construction, Inc. and SFR Recovery, Inc.", debarred for five years to 3/1/2026. Kin Wo Construction Inc is a separate registry account (0300631) that ended on 2020-12-31; Kwan Wo Ironworks Inc. (account 0913293, State licence 643621, clear) is still registered. 1 listed firm received City payments in a fiscal year after the year of the action: A&B Construction (Andrew M. Jordan, Inc.) ($10.1 million; agreed in a stipulation of 4 December 2023 not to take part in City contracting for three years).
how: Firms (not individuals) on the City's Suspended and Debarred Contractors page and in the Controller's semi-annual reports, with the earliest action date (the list built by the “earmarks” analysis), matched by exact normalised name to every member of every contract team in the Controller's Supplier Contracts table. A row is kept when the contract's term began after the action date. The amounts are the team member's own agreed and paid figures in that table. The names in the reports are read from the report text; the registry and licence records are matched on the same exact names.
limits: The table records the contract's start date, not the day the subcontractor was added or approved. The debarment order itself is not on disk, so the files do not show whether it named Kwan Wo Ironworks Inc. (and the reports misprint the name) or named the closed company Kin Wo Construction Inc. (and left the ironworks firm free to work). A prime contractor chooses its subcontractors; the files do not show whether Public Works reviewed the list against the debarment reports. A suspension ends when the proceeding ends, and a firm whose term has run may work again.
